newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals mostly higher early.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals mostly higher early.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were mostly higher early Tuesday on light volumes, with renewed tightness in the physical platinum group (PGM) metal market providing some support for the complex, traders said.
"There's no palladium available, and palladium lease rates are back above 50 percent, that's the whole story," one PGM dealer said.
The expiring NYMEX June palladium contract was up $8.20 at $176.00 an ounce, while the most-active NYMEX September palladium contract was up $3.70 an ounce at $168.00 early.

Palladium lending rates for the one month maturity in the physical market were quoted around 50 percent, up from around 30 percent Monday, while platinum lending rates for one month remained around 30 percent.
NYMEX July platinum was up $8.10 at $406.80 early.
Meanwhile, about 15 Japanese trade houses are reported to be in talks with Russian officials over a resumption of Russian PGM exports which have been suspended since last December.
Russia is the world's largest supplier of palladium, but the U.S. has now surpassed Japan as the leading consumer, according to a report lasd month by refiners Johnson Matthey.
Meanwhile, COMEX August gold was up 20 cents at $346.70 an ounce.
Spot gold was quoted was quoted $343.70/20 an ounce, compared to the London Tuesday morning fix at $343.80 and the New York close Monday around $343.30/70.

In news early Tuesday, the German government was reported to be backing down on its plan to force the Bundesbank to revalue its gold reserves and use the proceeds to help Germany meet the debt to GDP criteria for European Monetary Union (EMU).
COMEX July silver was up 3.2 cents at $4.730 an ounce.

In the bullion market, short term implied lease rates for silver rose further to around 4.00 percent for the one month maturity, from 2.6 percent Monday, as lending rates fell and LIBOR was steady. ((Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641))
